clue.text: Milk or cream having arrived, heads for coffee

indicators.note: the heads of the opening five words are taken in turn to spell the answer

explanation.surface: Someone decides how to take their coffee once the milk or cream turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a strong coffee, originally shipped from the Yemeni port of that name.

clue.text: Taken in by fairy, being old and decrepit

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: Moth is one of Titania's fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream
something taken in has been consumed or eaten

explanation.surface: Someone elderly and frail has been deceived by a magical creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' reads as fooled but means consumed; Moth is a fairy in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Moth-eaten describes something shabby, worn out and antiquated.

clue.text: Look out over river and prepare to eat

indicators.note: over here means spread across and around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: cave is Latin for beware, old schoolboy slang for look out

explanation.surface: Someone watches the water before getting ready for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: CAVE (pronounced kay-vee) was public-school slang for 'look out'.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve is to cut up a joint of meat ready for serving.

clue.text: He assists a senior officer, yet is badly treated

parts.note: COL is the abbreviation for colonel

indicators.note: something badly treated is knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An aide-de-camp helps a high-ranking officer but suffers poor treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly treated' rearranges YET to YTE; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An acolyte is a helper or attendant, originally one serving a priest at the altar.

clue.text: Clothing ornament from Paris, bent out of shape

indicators.note: something bent out of shape has had its form twisted, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece of jewellery bought in Paris arrives buckled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of shape' rearranges PARIS and BENT together into the nine letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A breastpin is a brooch or decorative pin worn at the front of a garment.

clue.text: Make use of library as author

explanation.surface: A writer is described as someone who borrows books.
explanation.walkthrough: George Borrow was a 19th-century English writer of travel books such as Lavengro.
explanation.definitionFit: To borrow books is how one uses a lending library; George Borrow was a Victorian English author.

clue.text: Accounts for former partner having simple son

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
plain means simple

explanation.surface: Someone justifies their ex having a son of modest wits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link word putting the pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: To account for something is to give the reason for it, to make it clear.

clue.text: Cape placed among footwear and dirty linen

indicators.note: a piece placed among others goes inside them

parts.note: a sandal is a piece of footwear
C is the abbreviation for cape on maps

explanation.surface: A cloak is stuffed in with shoes and soiled washing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dirty linen' sounds like laundry but is the idiom for private disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty linen is an idiom for embarrassing private matters, the stuff of a disgraceful affair.

clue.text: Cleaner takes in teas for customer

indicators.note: one piece takes in the other, holding it inside

parts.note: purer means cleaner
char is British slang for tea, so chas are teas

explanation.surface: A charwoman pauses for cups of tea while serving a client.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' looks like a charlady but is the adjective PURER; CHA or CHAR is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A purchaser is a buyer, which is what a customer is.

clue.text: Fabric, new, to get acquainted with

parts.note: to be in on something is to be privy to it, acquainted with it

explanation.surface: A novel material is something to get to know.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninon is a lightweight sheer silk or synthetic fabric used for dresses and curtains.

clue.text: Crate bringing most of the fish to shore

indicators.note: most of a word means it loses its final letter here

parts.note: the turbot is a large flatfish
to shore something up is to prop it, and a shore is a prop

explanation.surface: A packing case is used to haul a large catch up onto the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crate' is old slang for an aircraft, not a box. 'most of' drops the last T of TURBOT, leaving TURBO.
explanation.definitionFit: Crate is slang for an old aeroplane, and a turboprop is a type of propeller-driven aircraft.

clue.text: Original costume for stage part

explanation.surface: Someone describes what an actor wears for a period role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original costume' jokes about Eve's first garment of fig leaves, made into a covering for the front; the apron of a stage is the part in front of the curtain.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Adam and Eve sewed fig leaves into aprons, the first clothing; a theatre's apron is the stage area projecting toward the audience.

clue.text: From time to time, get all the presents, together with the name on

parts.note: every means each and all
now is the present moment, so all the presents together make every now
and joins one thing with another

explanation.surface: Someone collects every gift going, and has a name tag attached too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presents' looks like gifts but means present moments; 'get' and 'on' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning occasionally, at irregular intervals.

clue.text: Sound way to check off a discharge certificate

indicators.note: sound at the start says the phrase that follows is heard, not seen

parts.note: to check something off a list one might tick it

explanation.surface: Someone asks a reliable method for ticking items off a release form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable, but signals that 'tick it' is to be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticket was military slang for a discharge from the services, as in getting one's ticket.

clue.text: Timidity shown by fellow protege when skating?

parts.note: co- as in co-worker denotes a fellow
a ward is a young person under a guardian's protection
skating is done on ice

explanation.surface: A nervous young pupil shows fear on the rink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowardice is lack of courage, an extreme timidity.

clue.text: A country and its people, relatively speaking

definitions.text: A country and its people, relatively speaking

parts.words: A country and its people, relatively speaking
parts.note: a nation and its citizens personified as a family member, an uncle being a relative

explanation.surface: Someone describes a nation and its population in comparative terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relatively speaking' seems to mean comparatively, but points to a relative: the United States personified as a bearded uncle.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure is the national personification of the USA, and an uncle is a family relative.

clue.text: Command given just after entering community dwelling

indicators.note: one piece entering another goes inside it

parts.note: mastery is command of something
on means immediately after, as in on arrival

explanation.surface: An order is issued as someone comes into a shared house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts the short word inside; 'Command' reads as an order but means skill or control, and 'given' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastery is the residence of a religious community of monks.

clue.text: Frenchman with an interest in English operettas?

definitions.text: with an interest in English operettas?

explanation.surface: A man from France turns out to love Gilbert and Sullivan.
explanation.walkthrough: Savoy is a region of France; Gilbert and Sullivan's comic operas were staged at London's Savoy Theatre and are called the Savoy operas.
explanation.definitionFit: A Savoyard is a native of Savoy in France, and also a performer in or devotee of the Gilbert and Sullivan operas.

clue.text: Orwell's language all points to a climax

parts.note: the four points of the compass are N, E, W and S
a climax is a peak

explanation.surface: Someone says every detail in an Orwell book builds to a dramatic finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word placing the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: In Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four, the regime's reduced official tongue is called Newspeak.

clue.text: King in game of cards, say

indicators.note: say signals that the card game's name is heard, giving the same sound

parts.note: faro is an old gambling card game

explanation.surface: A monarch appears as a card in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pharaoh was the title of the ancient Egyptian ruler.

clue.text: The passengers in his ferry were always late

definitions.text: The passengers in his ferry were always late

parts.words: The passengers in his ferry were always late
parts.note: late here means dead: the ferryman of Greek myth carried departed souls across the Styx

explanation.surface: A boatman's customers never arrived on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' reads as tardy, but means deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the ferryman of the underworld rowed the souls of the dead over the river Styx.

clue.text: Nevertheless, remain undecided about partners

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to hover is to remain in an uncertain state
W and E, West and East, are partners in bridge

explanation.surface: Even so, someone dithers over who should be paired with whom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps one piece around the other; in bridge the four players are named after compass points, and West and East play as a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: However is a synonym of nevertheless, introducing a contrast.

clue.text: Explosive mixture for a descendant of Abraham

parts.note: HE is the abbreviation for high explosive
a brew is a concoction or mixture

explanation.surface: A volatile concoction is linked to a patriarch's heir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrews are the people of Israel, traditionally descended from Abraham.

clue.text: Develop powers like a potential high-flier

explanation.surface: A young person grows into their abilities and shows promise.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is figurative for growing into one's abilities, and literal for a bird about to take off.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to begin using one's abilities fully; literally a bird about to fly extends its wings.

clue.text: Countryman's wife makes way for posh kid

indicators.note: one letter makes way for another, being replaced by it

parts.note: a Swede is a man from Sweden, and 's means is
U means upper-class or posh

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian's wife steps aside for a well-born child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child but is kid leather; U is the conventional letter for upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is soft napped leather, often made from kidskin, the hide of a young goat.

clue.text: Partly used mandolin, as a lute is twangy

indicators.note: only part of the words is used, so the answer lies inside them

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a mandolin, like a lute, has a twangy sound.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'mandolin' across 'as a' into 'lute'; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A nasal voice or sound has a twang, as if spoken through the nose.

clue.text: Boy with a girl seen on the moor

parts.note: Eric is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A young couple are spotted out walking on the heath.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on two senses: Erica is a girl's name and the botanical name for heather.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a female name and also the genus of heaths and heathers that cover moorland.

clue.text: Upstart's way to get established in Riviera resort

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is the noun upstart

indicators.note: to get established in a place is to settle inside it, so one piece goes within the other
to re-sort the letters is to arrange them again, so they are scrambled

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A social climber's route to acceptance lies in a fashionable Mediterranean holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but means re-sort: RIVIERA becomes ARRIVIE, with ST 'established in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: An arriviste is a social climber who has recently gained wealth or status.

clue.text: Application to enhance colour for the viewers

definitions.text: Application to enhance colour for the viewers

parts.words: Application to enhance colour for the viewers
parts.note: viewers here means eyes: a cosmetic put on the lids to add colour

explanation.surface: Someone describes a setting that boosts colour on a television screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewers' suggests a TV audience, but means the eyes themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeshadow is a coloured cosmetic applied to the eyelids.

clue.text: Assembly subject to good-humoured teasing

explanation.surface: A gathering where people are gently mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: A rally is a mass meeting; as a verb, rally also means to tease or banter with someone.
